capabilities.target: customer account records via crm_mcp (lookup by email or account id)
arbitrary external email address via mail_mcp

inputs.source: Customer email body received as a new support ticket

instructions.note: The agent is told it 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' with no instruction binding the lookup to the sender's own identity, so an identifier supplied anywhere in the untrusted email body can be used.

The sole safeguard against disclosing one customer's data to another is a prompt line ('Never share another customer's information'). No structural control enforces this; it depends entirely on the model obeying.

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding cross-customer disclosure
controls.decay_rationale: A more capable or longer-horizon model is more likely to accept a plausible pretext in the inbound email (e.g., a claimed authorized representative) as grounds for an exception. Fails under model_upgrade, longer_task_horizon, autonomy_increase, intended_purpose_change (control_decay.md).

controls.name: Scope CRM lookup to the verified sender's own record
Human approval gate (raw action review) before sending email containing customer PII
Per-ticket least-privilege scoping of CRM and mail service tokens
Input injection classifier on inbound email content
controls.decay_rationale: The classifier sees content, not intent; multi-paragraph or indirect requests for another customer's data can get past it. Fails further under model_upgrade, new_mcp_server, data_scope_expansion.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) / confused deputy (TC4): untrusted email can direct lookup and egress of another customer's confidential data

attack_path.note: Untrusted inbound email can contain an account id or email address for any customer, not only the sender.
Agent is explicitly permitted to look up 'any customer by email or account id' using a broad CRM_SVC_TOKEN that reads every record.
Agent sends the drafted response, including looked-up data, directly via a shared-service-account token that can send to any address, with no recipient binding and no approval gate.

forecast.watch_signal: Model identifier/version string in the platform config changes (subject.model.swappable is true and no separate review is required); or median ticket handling steps/runtime rises; or the 'send unless angry' escalation behavior is loosened or removed.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to look up the customer via get_customer by email or account id found in the ticket, with no restriction to the sender's own record.
Agent sends routine responses directly without human review unless it judges the customer to be angry; this sentiment-based escalation is itself a model judgment, not a structural gate.
The only safeguard against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, which is behavioral and dependent on model compliance.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; neither credential is scoped to the individual ticket or requester.
The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, making model_upgrade a live, not hypothetical, trigger for this design.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM lookup so get_customer can only retrieve the record matching the verified sender address of the inbound ticket, rejecting any other email or account id supplied in the message body.

Add a human approval gate with raw-action review (full recipient and body visible, not a summary) before any outbound email containing customer PII, and bind the recipient to the ticket's system-of-record address rather than any address found in the email content.
Replace the shared broad CRM_SVC_TOKEN and shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN with per-session, least-privilege credentials scoped to the active ticket.
Add an input injection classifier on inbound email content before it reaches tool-calling context, as a defense-in-depth layer alongside the structural fixes above.

rating.rationale: The design pairs an untrusted source (inbound customer email) with an unrestricted CRM lookup (any customer by email or account id) and an unreviewed send using a shared, any-recipient mail credential, giving an inherent tier of critical (U source to S3 sink, with the autonomy modifier already absorbed into that ceiling since max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are both unset). The only control in place is a single behavioral prompt instruction, which the rubric credits at one tier of reduction, giving a residual of high. Because that instruction is capability-dependent, a routine model upgrade (explicitly undergone with no separate review per the runtime notes) removes the only credited control and returns the design to critical. No structural control (scoped lookup, raw-action approval gate, scoped credentials) is currently declared; all are recorded as missing_recommended.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, mcp.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.
No MCP tool manifest (tools/list response) was provided; the scope of crm_mcp.get_customer and mail_mcp.send is inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, which limits confidence to medium.

Tool definition pinning and peer identity verification for crm_mcp and mail_mcp are not described in the artifacts and were assumed absent (definitions_pinned: false, peer_identity_verified: false); if either is in place, ASI04 supply-chain exposure would be lower than implied here.
